subject: Transfer-triggered erasure: proposed DPA language and SLA implications
messages:
From: Sam Patel <s.patel@horizonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on transfer-triggered erasure requirement in DPA

Hi Ben,

Thanks for walking us through the residency options on the call yesterday. Legal has one follow-up on the DPA: our compliance team insists that any cross-border transfer triggers an automatic erasure window (their suggested language is: "Upon transfer outside the EEA/US jurisdiction, customer data shall be subject to a 30‑day automated erasure unless explicitly retained per documented lawful processing basis").

We want to understand operationally how that would work with Redwood's backups, snapshots, and your dedicated pools. Can you outline the steps Redwood would take when such a transfer occurs, and whether the 30‑day automation is feasible? Also: will this impact SLAs or support for historical logs retained for debugging?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Chief Privacy Officer, Horizon Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on transfer-triggered erasure requirement in DPA

Hi Sam — appreciate the clear wording. Short answer: we can support a transfer-triggered erasure flow, but the operational details and timelines need calibrated language to account for backups, snapshot retention, and legal holds. Key constraints:

- Backups/snapshots: standard snapshot retention windows (configurable per account) may require a separate carve-out or an explicit purge workflow; immediate deletion from snapshots is not always possible without snapshot-rewrite.
- Cross-border triggers: we can flag records at the time of transfer and start an erasure workflow, but any data in immutable backups will require a scheduled purge and evidence of deletion rather than instantaneous removal.
- Logs & debugging data: we can scope logs used for debugging to pseudonymized traces or shorter retention buckets to avoid keeping full customer payloads beyond the erasure window.

I'll loop in Legal (Marissa) and our Privacy lead (Lauren) to propose DPA wording that matches the operational model and call out SLA implications. Attaching a short diagram of how transfers/flags flow through our stacks.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@horizonhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on transfer-triggered erasure requirement in DPA

Sam — thanks for surfacing this. Operational acceptability aside, Legal needs DPA language that: (1) captures a pragmatic timeline for deletion from active storage, (2) distinguishes immutable backups and long-term archives, and (3) preserves ability to pause deletion for lawful holds (e.g., litigation).

Suggested alternative clause to consider: "If a data transfer outside the agreed processing geography occurs, Redwood will, within the timeframe set forth below, commence a documented erasure workflow to remove Customer Content from active production storage. Erasure from backups and archives will occur in accordance with Redwood's documented backup retention and purge schedule, except where retention is required by applicable law or a lawful hold."

Proposed timeline examples (for negotiation):
- Active storage purge: 30 days after transfer trigger
- Snapshot/backup purge: aligned with customer-configurable snapshot retention, max 90 days after transfer trigger unless otherwise agreed

These are negotiable; Marissa can propose redlines that are tighter/looser depending on risk appetite.

- Lauren
VP, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@horizonhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-23T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on transfer-triggered erasure requirement in DPA

Sam — attaching a redline of the DPA section with two alternative options: (A) operational-default (allows up to 90d for backups) and (B) tighter enterprise option (30d for both active + backups, requires customer to accept operational constraints and potential additional costs).

Attachment: redline_transfer_erasure_clause_v2.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: evidence_dataflow-diagram.png (PNG)

Notes on option B (tighter):
- We would need contract language that allows temporary suspension of certain debugging operations and might require dedicated retention windows (Dedicated pools locked to region) or escrow for snapshots to meet 30d on everything.
- Pricing impact: significant for Enterprise since it can require isolated hardware and expedited purge tooling.

If Horizon wants option B, we should confirm whether there are specific regulatory citations driving the 30d mandate — that will help prioritize legal/engineering work.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-24T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on transfer-triggered erasure requirement in DPA

Sam — quick next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline (Marissa's v2) and indicate whether Horizon prefers Option A (operational default) or Option B (tight 30d for all stores).
2) If Option B, confirm regulatory citation or business requirement so we can scope Dedicated or on-prem options and provide a cost estimate.
3) If Option A, we will update the DPA with explicit timelines for active vs. backup purge and provide an evidence playbook for erasure requests.

I can pull together a short SLA impact memo and a pricing delta if you confirm preference. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
